chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Abi Himmam Isma’il ibn Himam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Qazvan, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers that Ali (peace be upon them) said:
Whoever raises his aspirations shall do wrong.
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of prolonging one's hopes (amal) on a person's deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq places this saying of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) within the chapter on 'Raising Aspirations' (*Tawallud al-Amal*), highlighting how excessive attachment to worldly longevity leads to spiritual negligence and the delay of repentance. This concept is central to Shia ethical teachings, where *amal* (hope/aspiration) is distinguished from *tawakkul* (trust in God), warning that mistaking long life for security often results in a deterioration of one's deeds and readiness for the Hereafter.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-52 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Abi Himmam Isma’il ibn Himam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Qazvan, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers that Ali (MGB) said, “
Whoever raises his aspirations shall do wrong.”
